jobs.description:
TYPE OF RECRUITMENT

We welcome applications from everyone!

WHEN TO APPLY

We will be accepting online applications from Thursday, July 23, 2026
until the position is filled. First consideration will be given to applications received by August 6, 2026
.

Why Work For Us?

THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES

The County of Los Angeles serves a demographically and geographically diverse population of more than 10 million residents. Employing over 100,000 employees who work in roles as broad as law, civil engineering, public safety, healthcare, and human services, the County operates with a budget of $50.3 billion. The County is an Equal Opportunity and Fair Chance employer, committed to advancing inclusion and respecting the diversity in its workforce. It is a culturally diverse economic and cultural hub, driving major elements of the national and world economies. Los Angeles County is the center for arts, media, and entertainment - unlike anywhere else.

THE DEPARTMENT

The Chief Executive Office (CEO) is the County's central executive, strategic, and administrative agency, driving transformative change to improve the lives of its diverse constituents. CEO leads collective efforts with departments to advance the priorities established by the Board of Supervisors, including justice reform, healthcare integration, child protection, anti-racism, diversity and inclusion, and poverty reduction.

As the administrative agency responsible for the County's $50.3 billion budget, CEO handles specialized functions to lead and maximize the use of County assets; advocate the County's position on State and federal agendas; lead and implement the Countywide Strategic Plan; implement risk management strategies to mitigate financial loss; and convey the County's message through a variety of communication platforms.

THE ANTI-RACISM, DIVERSITY, AND INCLUSION INITIATIVE

ARDI's vision is for Los Angeles County to be a place where all residents are healthy, experience justice, and thrive. Its mission is to end structural racism and its consequences in Los Angeles County by boldly articulating an anti-racism policy agenda that advances equity and eliminates systemic barriers, sustains equitable and inclusive policy development, workforce culture, data analysis, and promotes equal access to resources for all Los Angeles County residents.

ARDI supports County departments and community stakeholders through:
Training and capacity building.
Data collection, analysis, and reporting.
Technical assistance and planning.
Policy analysis and development.
Community and stakeholder engagement.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Executive Director, Racial Equity will lead the Los Angeles County's enterprise racial equity strategy by providing executive leadership for the County’s Anti-Racism, Diversity, and Inclusion (ARDI) initiative and serving as the County’s principal advisor on organizational transformation, equity strategy, implementation, and systems change. Reporting within the Chief Executive Office, the Executive Director will provide vision, strategic direction, and operational leadership for countywide efforts to identify, address, and eliminate structural and systemic racism and advance equity and inclusion in the areas where the County has control or influence, including service delivery, policy development, budgeting, contracting and employment.

The Executive Director will work across County departments and with community-based organizations, residents, philanthropy, academic partners, local jurisdictions, and other stakeholders to advance an anti-racist policy agenda, promote equity and inclusion, build institutional capacity, strengthen accountability, and improve outcomes for all Los Angeles County residents. The position will lead a multidisciplinary team and ensure that ARDI's work remains data-informed, community-centered, and aligned with the priorities of the Board of Supervisors.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is a collaborative and credible executive leader with a demonstrated commitment to racial equity and inclusion and a deep understanding of the ways in which historic and present-day discrimination and systemic barriers affect communities, institutions, and public systems. The successful candidate will be able to translate vision into action, navigate a large and complex governmental environment, engage thoughtfully in difficult conversations, and build effective partnerships with stakeholders who bring varied perspectives and experiences.

The selected individual will bring strong policy, organizational, and operational judgment; the ability to use data and evaluation to guide strategy; and a record of developing and sustaining initiatives that advance systemic change. The Executive Director must be an effective communicator who can build trust, foster collaboration, and maintain momentum across a broad range of internal and external partners.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Provide executive leadership and strategic direction for the ARDI Initiative and the County's racial equity agenda, including leading Countywide implementation of the Racial Equity Strategic Plan.
Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of strategies designed to reduce racial disparities and address systemic barriers.
Coordinate countywide efforts to advance equitable and inclusive policy development, workforce culture, and data analysis, and promote equal access to resources, and institutional accountability.
Evaluate County policies, practices, operations, programs, and services through a racial equity lens and develop practical recommendations for improvement.
Build and maintain executive partnerships with Department Heads, Chief Deputies, and senior County leadership to strengthen organizational capacity, technical expertise, and accountability for equity-related goals.
Lead enterprise partnerships with philanthropy, academic institutions, federal and state agencies, community-based organizations, residents, local jurisdictions, and other public-sector partners to advance shared equity goals.
Lead the development and implementation of evaluation frameworks, accountability systems, performance measures, dashboards, and public reporting strategies to strengthen organizational performance, transparency, and continuous improvement across departments.
Guide the collection, analysis, and use of data to identify disparities, measure progress, and communicate outcomes.
Advise County leadership on strategic initiatives, Board motions, legislation, and policy implementation.
Develop policy recommendations and support legislative and administrative strategies that advance the County's anti-racism agenda and promotion of equity and inclusion.
Lead, develop, and evaluate staff while fostering a culture of collaboration, engagement, and accountability.
Represent ARDI and the Chief Executive Office before internal and external stakeholders, as appropriate.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor’s degree in public policy, social science, education, public administration, ethnic studies, human services, political science, law, or a closely related field, AND

Minimum of five years of professional experience directing initiatives for an organization, focused on designing and implementing comprehensive programs advancing diversity, equity, inclusion or equal access, fostering inclusive organizational cultures, and advancing equitable public policies, including at least two years in a managerial or supervisory capacity.

LICENSE: A valid California Class "C" driver's license or the ability to utilize an alternative method of transportation when needed to carry out job-related essential functions.

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

Significant experience designing, facilitating, and scaling evidence-based training, capacity building initiatives, and awareness programs rooted in anti-racism, inclusion, intersectional equity, accessibility, and systemic justice.
Demonstrated experience developing institutional learning frameworks, toolkits, and policy recommendations directly aligned with the strategic goals, metrics, and objectives of the Anti-racism, Diversity, and Inclusion (ARDI) Initiative.
An advanced degree in Ethnic Studies, Public Policy, Sociology, Social Justice, or a related field, with a documented focus on the critical analysis of systemic, structural, and institutional racism.
Demonstrated success in facilitating complex, high-stakes dialogues with policymakers, diverse community stakeholders, and cross-sector partners regarding institutional bias and removing systemic barriers contributing to inequities, with a proven track record of driving measurable organizational or cultural transformation.
Experience designing, implementing, and monitoring strategic interventions to mitigate systemic inequities and remove systemic barriers, including utilizing qualitative and quantitative metrics to evaluate the efficacy of equity initiatives.
Demonstrated knowledge of Los Angeles County’s unique governance structure, municipal landscape, and diverse demographic makeup, including an understanding of how historical regional policy decisions have impacted local communities.
Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, or evaluating policies, programs, or initiatives designed to reduce measurable disparities in outcomes for underrepresented, disadvantaged, or historically marginalized communities and individuals across multiple institutional systems.
Exceptional verbal communication, trauma-informed facilitation, and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex equity concepts into actionable insights for diverse audiences.

At KPMG, we are not only keeping pace with the future of business; we are defining it. Harnessing the full power of AI and digital innovation, we deliver intelligent, data-driven solutions to help our clients navigate change and transform their competitive edge. KPMG is currently seeking a Managing Director, Government Contract Compliance to join our Ethics and Compliance organization.

Responsibilities:

Lead the firms Government Contracts Compliance program, including governance, strategy and day-to-day oversight of regulatory compliance obligations
Maintain a comprehensive understanding of government contract regulatory requirements and emerging enforcement trends, translating changes into effective compliance program enhancements, policies, controls, training and business guidance
Oversee government contract compliance risk assessments, monitoring, testing and key risk indicator activities to assess program effectiveness and drive continuous improvement
Serve as the primary lead for government contract audits, regulatory examinations and audit readiness efforts, coordinating responses and remediation initiatives
Partner with business, legal, risk, independence, privacy and compliance stakeholders to embed compliance requirements into firm processes and operations
Prepare and deliver compliance risks, regulatory developments, control effectiveness, issue remediation and overall program performance to senior leadership and governance committees

Qualifications:

Minimum 10 years of recent experience leading regulatory compliance, government compliance, legal, risk management, internal audit, or related programs within a complex organization
Deep experience with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and agency subparts, Cost Accounting Standards (CAS), DFARS Business Systems and indirect cost rates and procurement statutes
Demonstrate experience managing the full lifecycle of DCAA audits, including incurred cost audits, business system audits (Accounting, Estimating and more) and forward pricing rate negotiations and experience working with government contract oversight and audit agencies including DCMA, DCAA and GSA
Profound knowledge of government contracts and regulatory compliance requirements, including compliance program governance, risk assessment, design, monitoring, testing and remediation practices
Demonstrated experience designing and operating risk-based compliance programs, including risk registers, controls, policies, training, monitoring activities and reporting mechanisms
Strong analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to synthesize complex regulatory content into executive messaging to senior leaders and partners across legal, risk, privacy, compliance and business functions

Farmer-first:
Everything we do is to help farmers lead in water quality and achieve successful conservation outcomes.
No box-checking:
Doing work for the sake of work doesn’t lead to change.
Filling gaps:
We look for ways to fill gaps and solve problems that others say “no” to.
Curiosity & experimentation:
Sometimes being innovative means failing. As long as we learn, it’s part of the process.

Translates complex agriculture, conservation and water quality issues into clear and effective communications for diverse audiences.
Identifies opportunities to grow IAWA's visibility, credibility, relationships and influence.
Guides the continued growth and development of IAWA's Conservation Compass.

Develops and manages the annual communications and engagement budget.
Collaborates across IAWA, Amplify, ISA and partner organizations to ensure communications and engagement efforts are coordinated and aligned.
Monitors emerging issues, opportunities and trends affecting IAWA, agriculture, conservation and water quality.
Supports organizational events, meetings and other activities as needed.

Ability to connect communications and engagement activities to organizational strategy, priorities, and desired outcomes.

Builds trust and productive relationships across diverse audiences, organizations, and perspectives.

Exceptional writing, editing, and storytelling skills with the ability to communicate complex topics clearly.

TYPE OF RECRUITMENT

We welcome applications from everyone!

WHEN TO APPLY

We will be accepting online applications from Thursday, July 23, 2026
until the position is filled. First consideration will be given to applications received by August 6, 2026
.

Why Work For Us?

THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES

The County of Los Angeles serves a demographically and geographically diverse population of more than 10 million residents. Employing over 100,000 employees who work in roles as broad as law, civil engineering, public safety, healthcare, and human services, the County operates with a budget of $50.3 billion. The County is an Equal Opportunity and Fair Chance employer, committed to advancing inclusion and respecting the diversity in its workforce. It is a culturally diverse economic and cultural hub, driving major elements of the national and world economies. Los Angeles County is the center for arts, media, and entertainment - unlike anywhere else.

THE DEPARTMENT

The Chief Executive Office (CEO) is the County's central executive, strategic, and administrative agency, driving transformative change to improve the lives of its diverse constituents. CEO leads collective efforts with departments to advance the priorities established by the Board of Supervisors, including justice reform, healthcare integration, child protection, anti-racism, diversity and inclusion, and poverty reduction.

As the administrative agency responsible for the County's $50.3 billion budget, CEO handles specialized functions to lead and maximize the use of County assets; advocate the County's position on State and federal agendas; lead and implement the Countywide Strategic Plan; implement risk management strategies to mitigate financial loss; and convey the County's message through a variety of communication platforms.

THE ANTI-RACISM, DIVERSITY, AND INCLUSION INITIATIVE

ARDI's vision is for Los Angeles County to be a place where all residents are healthy, experience justice, and thrive. Its mission is to end structural racism and its consequences in Los Angeles County by boldly articulating an anti-racism policy agenda that advances equity and eliminates systemic barriers, sustains equitable and inclusive policy development, workforce culture, data analysis, and promotes equal access to resources for all Los Angeles County residents.

ARDI supports County departments and community stakeholders through:
Training and capacity building.
Data collection, analysis, and reporting.
Technical assistance and planning.
Policy analysis and development.
Community and stakeholder engagement.

THE OPPORTUNITY

The Executive Director, Racial Equity will lead the Los Angeles County's enterprise racial equity strategy by providing executive leadership for the County’s Anti-Racism, Diversity, and Inclusion (ARDI) initiative and serving as the County’s principal advisor on organizational transformation, equity strategy, implementation, and systems change. Reporting within the Chief Executive Office, the Executive Director will provide vision, strategic direction, and operational leadership for countywide efforts to identify, address, and eliminate structural and systemic racism and advance equity and inclusion in the areas where the County has control or influence, including service delivery, policy development, budgeting, contracting and employment.

The Executive Director will work across County departments and with community-based organizations, residents, philanthropy, academic partners, local jurisdictions, and other stakeholders to advance an anti-racist policy agenda, promote equity and inclusion, build institutional capacity, strengthen accountability, and improve outcomes for all Los Angeles County residents. The position will lead a multidisciplinary team and ensure that ARDI's work remains data-informed, community-centered, and aligned with the priorities of the Board of Supervisors.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative and credible executive leader with a demonstrated commitment to racial equity and inclusion and a deep understanding of the ways in which historic and present-day discrimination and systemic barriers affect communities, institutions, and public systems. The successful candidate will be able to translate vision into action, navigate a large and complex governmental environment, engage thoughtfully in difficult conversations, and build effective partnerships with stakeholders who bring varied perspectives and experiences.

The selected individual will bring strong policy, organizational, and operational judgment; the ability to use data and evaluation to guide strategy; and a record of developing and sustaining initiatives that advance systemic change. The Executive Director must be an effective communicator who can build trust, foster collaboration, and maintain momentum across a broad range of internal and external partners.

Provide executive leadership and strategic direction for the ARDI Initiative and the County's racial equity agenda, including leading Countywide implementation of the Racial Equity Strategic Plan.
Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of strategies designed to reduce racial disparities and address systemic barriers.
Coordinate countywide efforts to advance equitable and inclusive policy development, workforce culture, and data analysis, and promote equal access to resources, and institutional accountability.
Evaluate County policies, practices, operations, programs, and services through a racial equity lens and develop practical recommendations for improvement.
Build and maintain executive partnerships with Department Heads, Chief Deputies, and senior County leadership to strengthen organizational capacity, technical expertise, and accountability for equity-related goals.
Lead enterprise partnerships with philanthropy, academic institutions, federal and state agencies, community-based organizations, residents, local jurisdictions, and other public-sector partners to advance shared equity goals.
Lead the development and implementation of evaluation frameworks, accountability systems, performance measures, dashboards, and public reporting strategies to strengthen organizational performance, transparency, and continuous improvement across departments.
Guide the collection, analysis, and use of data to identify disparities, measure progress, and communicate outcomes.
Advise County leadership on strategic initiatives, Board motions, legislation, and policy implementation.
Develop policy recommendations and support legislative and administrative strategies that advance the County's anti-racism agenda and promotion of equity and inclusion.
Lead, develop, and evaluate staff while fostering a culture of collaboration, engagement, and accountability.
Represent ARDI and the Chief Executive Office before internal and external stakeholders, as appropriate.

Graduation from an accredited college or university with a bachelor’s degree in public policy, social science, education, public administration, ethnic studies, human services, political science, law, or a closely related field, AND

Minimum of five years of professional experience directing initiatives for an organization, focused on designing and implementing comprehensive programs advancing diversity, equity, inclusion or equal access, fostering inclusive organizational cultures, and advancing equitable public policies, including at least two years in a managerial or supervisory capacity.

Farmer-first:
Everything we do is to help farmers lead in water quality and achieve successful conservation outcomes.
No box-checking:
Doing work for the sake of work doesn’t lead to change.
Filling gaps:
We look for ways to fill gaps and solve problems that others say “no” to.

Sometimes being innovative means failing. As long as we learn, it’s part of the process.

The Digital Communication Services role is a critical element of the Technology Services directorate.

Operational performance, incident leadership and service assurance across business-critical services

People leadership, capability development and organisational culture across multidisciplinary teams
Senior stakeholder engagement and cross-MoJ coordination to enable coherent, end-to-end service delivery.

Proven senior leadership of large-scale technology services with significant operational and reputational impact.
